title: Tenali Raman and the Stolen Royal Peacocks

full_text:
Three magnificent royal white peacocks, gifted to Queen Tirumala Devi by the King of Ceylon, disappeared from the royal aviary inside the palace gardens. The peacocks were pure white, with magnificent snow-colored plumage and blue eyes.
A rumor spread that a corrupt animal dealer named Bhima had stolen them and concealed them in his private farm outside the city.

The royal guards raided Bhima’s farm, but found only thirty common, mottled grey-and-green farm geese and brown turkeys in the pens.
Bhima laughed: 'Look around! I have no white peacocks! The guards are harassing an honest farmer!'

The captain was about to leave when Tenali Raman arrived at the farm.
Tenali looked at a large, windowless wooden barn in the center of the compound, locked with three iron padlocks.
Bhima said: 'That barn holds only sacks of dry onions and garlic; opening it will spoil the crop!'

Tenali did not break the locks.
He knew that peacocks possess an intense, instinctual reaction to the arrival of rain and thunder, spreading their plumage and emitting their distinctive, loud, ringing trumpet call: *‘MAY-AWE! MAY-AWE!’*

Tenali instructed two royal drummers, who had accompanied the guards, to set up two massive war drums (*nagaras*) outside the closed barn.
Tenali signaled the drummers:
The drummers struck the heavy drumheads with furious, rhythmic power, producing a deep, reverberating rumble that shook the ground, perfectly imitating the thunderclaps of a monsoon thunderstorm!
At the same time, Tenali’s servants tossed buckets of water onto the barn's tin roof to mimic torrential rain!

The moment the rhythmic thunder and rain sound echoed inside the dark barn, the birds inside responded to their nature!
From inside the locked barn came three unmistakable, loud, piercing, trumpet calls:
*‘MAY-AWE! MAY-AWE! MAY-AWE!’*
And the distinct, heavy rustling of massive white feathers fanning against the wooden walls was heard by everyone present!

Tenali turned to the police captain:
'Break down the doors! The onions are singing royal peacock hymns!'

The guards smashed open the doors:
There, standing inside a hidden straw pen, were the Queen's three pure-white peacocks, their magnificent snow-white tails fully fanned in response to the false thunder!

Bhima collapsed in terror, confessing his theft.
The white peacocks were returned safely to the Queen’s aviary, Bhima was imprisoned, and the King marveled at Tenali’s ingenious use of animal psychology to make the victims announce their own rescue.
moral: Nature's distinct calls and habits cannot be concealed; truth sounds its own fanfare.
